summary: Gone L-4 cabin on Steamboat Mountain in the Lewis and Clark National Forest: built 1933 or 1934, abandoned 1973; no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: L-4 cab: wood, painted white, about 14 by 14 feet and 14 feet tall (1960 survey description)
facts.status_note: FireLookout.com says abandoned 1973 and gone; the Forest Fire Lookout Association Montana list also marks it gone

events.note: Work under way by June 19, 1930 (trail crew at work toward the planned station on the summit); trail and forest telephone line completed to the lookout camp by August 28, 1930
Independent Record item dated December 15, 1933 reports a new lookout house built; FireLookout.com dates its L-4 cab to 1934
FireLookout.com lists the cabin as abandoned in 1973

evidence.supports: location given as 17 miles southwest of Augusta
ranger Harris had a crew building the trail to the new station (June 19, 1930 item)
evidence.quote: Ranger Harris has a crew of men at work building a trail around Steam-boat Mountain.

evidence.supports: trail's purpose was access to the planned station on the summit
evidence.quote: The purpose of this trail is to have access to the new look-out station to be placed on the top of Steam-boat Mountain.

evidence.supports: forest telephone line under construction from Elk Creek ranger station in July 1930
evidence.quote: He also inspected the new forest telephone line which is in process of construction from the Elk creek ranger station to Steamboat mountain.

evidence.supports: trail and telephone line completed to the lookout camp (August 28, 1930 item)
evidence.quote: The trail and the telephone line have been completed to the lookout camp on the top of Steamboat Mountain.

evidence.supports: Independent Record item reporting a new lookout house built, December 15, 1933
evidence.quote: December 15, 1933: A new lookout house has been built at Steamboat mountain in the Sun river district.

evidence.supports: 1960 survey places the summit 13 miles south and 12 miles east of Augusta
evidence.quote: LOCATED 13 MILES SOUTH AND 12 MILES EAST OF AUGUSTA, 10 MILES

evidence.supports: 1960 survey described by Coast and Geodetic Survey
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1960 (OSR)
THE LOOKOUT IS CONSTRUCTED OF WOOD, PAINTED WHITE AND IS
APPROXIMATELY 14 X 14 FEET SQUARE. ITS HEIGHT, OVERALL, IS
Steamboat Mountain Lewis & Clark 47.30687 -112.64683 Ground Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Independent Record item (quoted by Forest Lookouts) reports the house built by December 15, 1933; FireLookout.com dates the L-4 cab to 1934. Both are kept in the events and the story; the year is not settled.

FireLookout.com says 17 miles southwest of Augusta; the 1960 survey description says 13 miles south and 12 miles east of Augusta, which is southeast. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Two sources disagree on the build year (1933 newspaper item vs 1934 on FireLookout.com) and on the direction from Augusta (southwest vs southeast). The 1930 to 1933 items are read through the Forest Lookouts page, not from the original Augusta News, Choteau Acantha or Independent Record. The FFLA record and both site pages confirm gone, but no source describes the summit today. No usable photo URL was found.
